# arrowlane-zig

> A pure Zig implementation of the arrowlane wire frame and lane selector.

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md): build, status and frame layout.
- [docs/ai/manifest.json](docs/ai/manifest.json): machine-readable capabilities and limits.
- [docs/ai/quickstart.md](docs/ai/quickstart.md): build and first command.
- [docs/ai/api.md](docs/ai/api.md): implemented calls and limits.
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): private reporting route.

## Current boundary

Implemented: frame encode/decode, general schema reader/writer for common
types, canonical eight-column JSON, IPC and ipc-zstd fixtures, one-field int64
IPC spike, fixture chunk streams, selector, C ABI, POSIX shm fixture lane,
`bench`, parser fuzz targets and `describe`.

Not implemented: general JSON lane, general IPC lane, general record batch
codec. The shm lane is POSIX only on Linux and macOS, and has no CLI
command.

The manifest reports `"shm":"fixture-posix"` and marks the general record paths
as fixture scoped. Do not treat the fixture path as a general Arrow table codec.

## Commands

- `zig build`
- `zig build test`
- `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe`
- `zig build fuzz` on Linux only: deterministic 10,000-input mutation
  gate over frame, shm descriptor and schema parsers
- `bash scripts/gate.sh`
- `zig-out/bin/arrowlane-zig describe`
- `zig-out/bin/arrowlane-zig --version`
- `zig-out/bin/arrowlane-zig bench --rows 200000 --repeats 5`

## Performance

JSON is the clear Zig win. IPC and ipc-zstd are correct but slower than Python
and Rust. arrow-cpp is the reference implementation that wins the IPC lanes.
See `docs/performance.md`.
